newsitem.title: UK: British villain Kray salutes dead twin with fly-by.
newsitem.headline: British villain Kray salutes dead twin with fly-by.

text.p: Britain's most notorious gangster, Reggie Kray, organised a birthday fly-by over his late twin's grave on Thursday from his prison cell.

Ronnie Kray, a paranoid schizophrenic, died in March 1995, aged 61. Hundreds of people lined the streets of the working class East End of London to watch black-plumed horses pull the hearse carrying his coffin to the cemetery in Chingford.
On Thursday, two light planes flew over the graveyard and a banner unfurled behind one of them proclaiming: "Ronald Kray: Never to be forgotten".

The same phrase is carved on his tombstone, under the word "Legend" alongside a photo of Ronnie from his younger days, when the sharp-suited Kray twins ruled London's gangland and rubbed shoulders with celebrities in the capital's night clubs.
After a crime career that included Reggie killing Jack "The Hat" McVitie, they were both sentenced to life imprisonment in 1969 for murder.
Reggie, 63 on Thursday, is still in jail, and all 20 or so bystanders at the cemetery thought it was time he was out.
Les Martin, who is leading a campaign to get Reggie parole, thought the government could release him as early as Christmas, if only he would "show a bit more remorse".
"He would be an ambassador for crime," Martin said, alarmingly. It turned out he meant crime prevention.
"He would talk about the dangers of crime. He loves kids. He'd tell them: "Look what it's done to me'," Martin said.
Eileen Sheridan-Price, "Friend of the Krays" and "The First Miss United Kingdom, 1958" according to her visiting card, also saw Reggie as a law-enforcer, in his own way.
"The Krays were something to look up to. They only harmed their own type. Your grandmothers were safe then," she said.
She had recently visited Reggie in prison. "He's in terrific form, mentally and physically, and he's still very handsome. You wouldn't mess with him," she said.
Reggie will not be kicking his heels in his cell on his birthday. He is the best man at the wedding in prison of a fellow prisoner, Bradley Allardyce.
"Bradley and Donna" had sent a floral tribute to Ronnie's grave, white flowers on white silk spelling out "Godfather 1".
Elder brother Charlie Kray, 70, could not be present.

He is currently in prison facing a drug trafficking charge and according to John, who declined to give his surname but said he worked "in security" with Charlie, he was likely to be remanded for another two weeks at a hearing on Thursday.
Posted on the new Kray Twins Internet site, launched on Thursday, was a letter sent to Charlie from Reggie, who said he was devastated to hear of his arrest.
Reggie made no reference to the alleged offence, but he told Charlie in his letter the police had been "polite and helpful" as he desperately sought news of his plight.
